content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe different methods of waste disposal
Explain the benefits and problems of recycling different materials
Describe the recycling process for metals, glass, and plastics
Discuss the concept of a circular economy
Modern society produces vast amounts of waste. Managing this waste is a major environmental challenge. The traditional approach of landfill is increasingly unsustainable, making
and other waste reduction strategies essential.
- Don't create waste in the first place
- Use items again for same or different purpose
- Process materials to make new products
[DIAGRAM: Waste hierarchy pyramid with Prevention at top, Disposal at bottom]
Much less than extracting from ore
Why aluminium recycling is particularly valuable:
Extracting aluminium from bauxite requires electrolysis
This uses enormous amounts of electricity
Recycling uses only 5% of this energy
Aluminium can be recycled indefinitely without quality loss
Don't break down in landfill or ocean
[DIAGRAM: Circular economy showing materials cycling back through design, production, use, and recycling]
Explain why recycling aluminium is more beneficial than recycling steel.
Both are beneficial, but aluminium recycling saves more energy:
This uses enormous amounts of electricity
Recycling saves about 95% of this energy
Recycled aluminium is identical in quality to new
Extraction from iron ore uses blast furnaces
High temperatures but less electricity than electrolysis
Recycling saves about 70% of extraction energy
Aluminium recycling saves more energy proportionally
Aluminium is lighter so transport emissions are lower
Both should be recycled whenever possible
Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of recycling plastics.
Reduces plastic in landfill and oceans
Conserves oil resources (plastics made from crude oil)
Reduces need for new plastic production
Many different plastic types that can't mix
Some plastics can only be recycled once or twice
Collection and transport have their own emissions
Explain what is meant by a 'circular economy'.
Materials kept in use as long as possible
Products are shared, leased, reused, repaired
Thinking all plastics can be recycled together
Different plastic types usually can't be mixed
Assuming recycling is always better than reuse
Reuse is higher in the waste hierarchy than recycling
Thinking biodegradable plastics solve the problem
They need specific conditions and can contaminate recycling
List the waste hierarchy in order of preference. (2 marks)
Explain two problems with disposing of waste in landfill sites. (4 marks)
Explain why recycling aluminium saves significant amounts of energy. (3 marks)
Describe the challenges of recycling plastic. (4 marks)
Explain what is meant by a 'circular economy' and give two examples of its principles. (4 marks)
Compare the advantages and disadvantages of incineration versus landfill. (4 marks)
Order of preference for waste management
Economic system designed to eliminate waste
Evaluation of environmental impact from production to disposal
Land use, pollution, methane, long-term legacy
Challenged by many types, contamination, quality loss
Design out waste, keep materials in use, regenerate systems
Move from linear "take-make-dispose" to circular economy
